impact: app/Actions/Tests/AsAuthenticatedTest.php exits 2 with no output at all - no test names, no failure, no summary - so it takes the App suite's reporting down with it. The file calls Auth::guard('api')->login($user), and auth.guards.api is not defined in this application (php artisan config:show auth.guards.api errors). Resolving an undefined guard throws during the test body in a way Pest cannot report, which is why the run dies mute rather than failing. Decide whether the Actions framework's authenticated decorator is meant to support a named guard at all: if yes, define auth.guards.api and keep the test; if no, the test should exercise the default guard. Separately, the file created users through User::factory() with no RefreshDatabase - added in this commit, since without it those rows leak into the testing database.
resolution:
Resolved, but the diagnosis in the report was wrong about the cause, and the real one is worse than a test bug.

**The mute death was `exit`, not the undefined guard.** `AuthenticatedDecorator::handleUnauthenticated()` ended the non-JSON branch with `redirect()->route($route)->send(); exit;`. Confirmed directly: constructing the decorator unauthenticated and calling handle() printed the marker before it, dumped the redirect HTML to stdout, and never reached the marker after — the process was gone. That is why the file exited 2 with zero bytes: nothing crashed, the runner was terminated mid-test. The undefined `api` guard is real and fixed too, but it sits in test 3, while test 2 ('rejects unauthenticated users') hit `exit` and would have silenced the run on its own.

This was not a test-only defect. Any action using AsAuthenticated, invoked unauthenticated from a queue worker or console command, hard-kills the process mid-job; `exit` after `send()` also skips terminable middleware and the rest of the response lifecycle. Now throws `HttpResponseException(redirect()->route($route))` — the framework's supported way to return a response from deep in the stack: an HTTP request still gets the same redirect via the handler, and everywhere else it is an ordinary catchable exception.

**Second defect: every documented hook was uncallable.** `DecorateActions::hasMethod()` uses `method_exists()`, which ignores visibility, while `callMethod()` used `call_user_func_array()` from the decorator's scope. A `protected` hook therefore passed the guard and then died in the base class's `__call` with "Method ... does not exist" — for a method that plainly exists. AsAuthenticated's own docblocks document `getAuthGuard()`, `getAuthRedirectRoute()` and `handleUnauthenticated()` as `protected`, so the documented usage was exactly the broken usage, across every decorator. `callMethod()` now invokes through ReflectionMethod when the method really exists, keeping the `call_user_func_array()` path for names that do not (which is what `__call` legitimately serves). Fixed in the shared trait rather than by making one test action's method public, since the same trap applied to all ~30 decorators.

**The named-guard question the issue asked:** yes, it is intended — the decorator supports both a `$authGuard` property and a `getAuthGuard()` hook, and there is an AuthenticatedDesignPattern behind it. So `config/auth.php` was NOT changed: the application genuinely has no `api` guard, and adding one so a test can pass would be backwards. The test defines the guard for its own duration instead. Added a companion test asserting that a user authenticated only on the DEFAULT guard is still rejected — without it the original test would pass just as happily if the decorator ignored `$authGuard` entirely, which is the "green but checking nothing" trap.

Verified:
- app/Actions/Tests/AsAuthenticatedTest.php: 5 passed (was: exit 2, zero bytes of output).
- The App suite now reports a full summary — 53 failed, 8 skipped, 103 passed — where it previously produced none. Those 53 are pre-existing and unrelated; they match a per-file baseline taken before any change here, file for file.
- All 20 other app/Actions/Tests files and app/Actions/Decorators/tests (11 passed) are identical to that baseline, confirming the shared-trait change caused no regressions.
- `vendor/bin/pint --dirty` clean.

Filed separately: ISS-022 (RefreshDatabase migrations intermittently deadlock against dply_testing — environmental, makes any RefreshDatabase run non-deterministic).
title: AsAuthenticatedTest kills the runner silently: it logs into an 'api' guard that does not exist
